|Algorithm name|First Come First Serve (FCFS)|
|--|--|
|Algorithm idea|Mainly considered from the perspective of "fairness" (similar to the example of queuing to buy things in our daily life)|
|Algorithm rule|Serve according to the **order of arrival** of jobs/processes|
|Used for job/process scheduling|When used for **job scheduling**, it considers which job arrives first in the **backing queue**; ⟦MC_7a1718a3cc58b985_4⟧when used for **process scheduling**, it considers which process arrives first in the **ready queue**|
|Preemptive or not|Non-preemptive algorithm|
|Advantages and disadvantages|Advantages: fair, simple to implement; ⟦MC_7a1718a3cc58b985_5⟧Disadvantages: short jobs (processes) queued behind long jobs (processes) need to wait for a long time, and the weighted turnaround time is large, so the user experience is poor for short jobs. That is, **the FCFS algorithm is advantageous to long jobs and disadvantageous to short jobs**|
|Causes starvation|No|
